about: Cases for the three acts a reader makes on a data block written in a booklet: add a row (with `under` for a child), remove a row, and replace a field's value. Each case is a whole booklet text, one act, and either the whole booklet text after the act or the reason it was refused. One file, read by the renderer's test (test/applyvectors.test.js) and copied by any other writer that applies these acts, to run the same cases against its own code.
The expected answers were made by running the Booklet plugin for Obsidian's own code (core/apply.ts: applyInFence with applyAdd, applyDelete and applyAct), so the file records what the plugin does.

A case: `name`; `text` (the booklet); `pad` (optional: replace every `@PAD@` in `text` and in `act` with this many `x` first, to make a big block without a big file; the expected text holds the token in the same places, so expand it there too); `act`; `expect`; `spec` (optional, see Size).

`act` is one of `{kind:"add", in, module, pick, under?, row}`, `{kind:"delete", in, module, pick, was}` or `{kind:"edit", in, module, pick, field, was, a, eq}`. `in` is the id of the data block and `module` the id of the module it stands in (null for a block outside every module fence, as in a data section). `under` is the parent's id, left out for a top row. `eq` is how the data's value is compared with `was`: `value` (words trimmed, a number as digits) or `option` (a choice: words trimmed and case ignored).

`expect` is `{text}` (the booklet after the act, byte for byte; `same: true` too when it is the booklet unchanged, an act already applied) or `{refused}` with the word of the refusal: `no row`, `ambiguous`, `no field`, `changed`, `unreadable`, `identity`, `no place`, `not utf8`, `clash`, `too big` or `no write` (the block is not in the booklet's own text).

Size: SPEC.md section 5 ("What stops it") says the data is left alone when the changed file would be larger than a reader reads (5 MB). The plugin applies no limit to a block written in the booklet (only its data-file path has one), so the cases that pass 5 MB carry `expect` (what the plugin does: it writes) and `spec` (`{refused:"too big"}`, what SPEC says and the renderer does: the whole booklet's new text (for data written in the booklet the changed file is the booklet) may not be longer than `limit` bytes of UTF-8). A writer that holds to SPEC checks `spec` when a case has one. An act that changes nothing is not held to it.

Lines: a line ends at a line feed, with or without the carriage return before it. A carriage return alone does not end a line (the plugin's `splitLines`), so a writer must find the fences and the data block in that reading of the file; SPEC.md is silent on a lone carriage return.
Comments: a data fence that starts inside a comment (`<!-- -->` or `%% %%`, closed), a `<pre>` block or a `$$` block is part of it, not a block (the plugin's `visibleLines`); no write is made there.

A writer is expected to change only the bytes between the fences: the booklet before and after differ inside the block's fences and nowhere else, which every case shows because `expect.text` is the whole booklet.
